item.text:
**7B.4 Research Note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, 2024**

Bottom line: I found strong structural evidence that Egypt under Sisi kept state- and military-linked economic actors in privileged positions in 2024, but I did not find a reliable 2024 source tying Sisi or a close family member to a specific personal asset, bribe, shell company, or contract trail. The evidence is mostly about regime-linked privilege, opacity, and incomplete reform, not a direct forensic money trail.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Egypt - United States Department of State | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/ | The report says SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy significant advantages, including relief from regulatory requirements and, until recently, tax exemptions; some firms also hold exclusive rights over public assets and often do not publish regular financial statements. This is strong structural evidence that office-linked entities can profit through monopolies, exemptions, and opacity. | 7B.4, 7B.3 |
| Improving the business climate to revive private sector growth: OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024 | OECD | 2024 | https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html | OECD says military-owned firms benefit from tax and land/resource advantages, that ownership and management selection is opaque, and that public ownership structures are not transparent. This is the clearest 2024 evidence that regime-connected economic privilege remained entrenched. | 7B.4, 7B.3 |
| Egypt cabinet approves ending state enterprise tax privileges | Reuters via L’Orient Today | Jan. 31, 2024 | https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1366481/egypt-cabinet-approves-ending-state-enterprise-tax-privileges-.html | Egypt approved regulations to abolish many tax and fee exemptions for state-owned enterprises, which was a genuine anti-privilege move. But the rules still excluded military work and national-security activities, so the reform was partial rather than a clean break from preferential treatment. | 7B.4 |
| Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says corruption is pervasive, Sisi controls the Administrative Control Authority, and it lacks credibility, transparency, and the ability to monitor the military’s economic activities. That supports a finding that safeguards against self-dealing and hidden conflicts of interest were weak. | 7B.4 |

Search gap:
- I did not find reliable 2024 reporting that directly identified a named Sisi family member receiving a specific asset, contract, bribe, gift, or offshore holding tied to office.
- The strongest 2024 material is structural: military/state economic privilege, opaque ownership, and only partial reform.
